svg.text: Compile each user's posts into one corpus
illustrative text, not a real user

text.tspan: can't sleep again. third night in a row
at a sunny café table with pancakes and coffee.
new job starts monday, wish me luck

svg.text: 10 or more posts per user, in shuffled order (seed 42). No profile or demographic fields.
Insert the corpus into one task prompt

text.tspan: You are an expert supervisor evaluating suicide-risk signals in social media language.
Input: a collection of Facebook posts authored by a single user. (order is arbitrary)
[...] isolation, burden, emotional pain, entrapment, hopelessness, death, self-harm [...]
Remember that majority of users do not have suicidal ideation, do not overinterpret
posts that are not overtly suicidal.

svg.text: ← the corpus from step 1 goes here

text.tspan: Prediction: RISK=<1 for elevated risk, 0 for low risk>

svg.text: Greedy decoding in one generate() pass, with
forward hooks on the tapped layers
Qwen3 and DeepSeek-R1 reason before answering,
up to 512 new tokens. Gemma and Llama get 256
32k-token context. Longer corpora are split at
post boundaries and the chunks' vectors
Read hidden states at four token positions
prompt, read in one forward pass
Tapped layers (dots) along the model's depth
4 + 4 + 2 + 4 = 14 model-layer blocks × 4 positions = 56 vectors per user
attention fusion, fit on each training fold
Trained through a temporary linear probe that predicts high risk: weighted BCE (positive weight 1.5 × negatives / positives), full-batch Adam, learning rate 0.01, at most 500
epochs, keeping the epoch with the best development AUC (patience 50). The probe is then dropped. The weights pick among the 4 positions, not among tokens.
Classify with two networks on the same 1024 features
single task, best setting per fold
a different setting on each fold
multi-task cascade, one setting for all folds
P(high risk) from the suicide logit · mean test AUC 0.738
150 questionnaire-only epochs, then joint training (shared layer at 1/5 the lr). Scores use a moving average of the weights.
Setting: 1 × 512 shared, tanh, RMSprop lr 1e-4, 512-unit stages. 3 seeds × 5 best development-AUC epochs, averaged.
Loss: BCE on high risk + 4 × MSE on each z-scored questionnaire score.
5 stratified folds; every user is a test user exactly once
504-setting grid: 1–3 layers, 16–1024 units, tanh or sigmoid, learning rate
STM: best development AUC on each fold. MTM: aux-pretrained, then joint; pick by
typical (median) development AUC, not a lucky epoch.
Test folds are scored once, after selection.
